body: can you give a synthetic dataset / sniplet where this is a problem?
Suggestion: This line could be `proba[proba < np.finfo(proba.dtype).eps] = np.finfo(proba.dtype).eps`. I can make a PR for that if there's not a good reason for the 1e-5 minimum.

I'm in favor of what @stephen-hoover proposes. (If in C/C++, I'd use DBL_MIN.)

I can pose a simple, sort of degenerate, example. Suppose a two-tree AdaBoosted Decision Tree classifier for a two-class problem. Suppose that for some feature vector the terminal leaves have probabilities $p^{1} = [1.0 - 1e-6, 1.0e-6]$ and $p^{2} = [0.0, 1.0]$ for the first and second tree, respectively. With the current thresholding, the 0-probability in the second tree will be bumped to 1e-5 and the resulting ensemble classifier will choose the "wrong" answer.
It would be cool to come up with an actual regression test. I understand the problem, I was just hoping for a data example.

Unfortunately I don't have anything immediately available. If I had a bit more time (about to leave on vacation), I'd create something based on the toy example I provided. I can do so when I return if it would help. I actually encountered the problem in a very complicated way. I'd ported my classifier to C++ by writing code to generate the C++ files from my Python classifier, even duplicating the subject threshold rule. I found that the exact same feature vector data could produce slightly different decision function values, on the order of 1e-3, dependent upon where in my C++ code I called it. I traced those differences down to a tree that had a terminal probability for one class of about 1e-18. Altering the thresholding resolved the inconsistencies I was observing.
I will write up this PR, and I'll see if I can come up with a test case of some kind.

Tangentially related question: Why does `_samme_proba` take "n_classes" as an input? The output of `predict_proba` has shape (n_examples, n_classes). Taking an extra n_classes input seems unnecessary. Is that something I could / should change with the same PR?
I prefer doing a single thing in a PR.

issue.title: [MRG+2] BUG Use epsilon threshold in `_samme_proba`
issue.body:
The `ensemble.weight_boosting._samme_proba` function should preserve ordering of class probabilities within an example, but thresholding logic (to avoid taking the log of values <= 0) was disrupting this. Instead of thresholding `proba < 0` probabilities to 1e-5, threshold `proba < epsilon` to epsilon. This avoids the issue of, e.g., probability values of 0 becoming larger than values of 1e-7.

Add a unit test for `_samme_proba` which checks that probability ordering is unchanged. This test fails on the un-modified version of `_samme_proba`. 

Resolves issue #4944 .

body: Not sure about the `n_classes`, should not be needed.
There is no good reason for 1e-5. @stephen-hoover has the better solution. Thanks!
This issue has been resolved by #4967 and can be closed.
